title: Historical plain GRU recipe audit
head: a52ccafb01a6ceb9cbef46bdde381d3fed31ae78
scope: Read-only source and metadata review. No fitting, GPU, SSH, network changes, source edits, or checkpoint/large-array reads.

protocol.future_primary: Official chronological train-only fit, then independent official valid; preserve whole sequences. Learned preprocessing, teachers, caches and initializers must have fitting-only ancestry.
protocol.historical_rule: Keep old frozen recipes/results historical. Old component-fold, train+valid, random, public, and proxy scores are not current primary validation evidence.
protocol.identifier_rule: seq_ix and Parquet order do not establish timestamp chronology; require actual order evidence for any further chronological split.

sources.excerpt: Fit only on the earlier training partition; evaluate on the later independent validation partition.
Preserve historical recipes and label old folds historical.

answer_summary: Among inspected history, the most useful reproducible plain-GRU baselines are the H256x2 scratch recipe and its warm-start student variants, plus the exact H384 HPO trial 35 record. Their metrics come from old component folds whose fit ancestry included official-valid members, so none is a current train-only chronological result. The largest scalar found (.71815) is a narrow strict425 branch result with uncertified ancestry and no public/private estimate. The best traced public report is a three-member TL3 submission at .66832. The original GALAM architecture and recipe remain unknown; plain-GRU settings are not validated GALAM-GRU settings.

top6_findings.finding: No inspected historical result qualifies as official train-only chronological primary validation.

evidence.excerpt: Fit only on training; seq_ix is not timestamp order.
No actual-data chronology audit or exact reference identity is claimed.

top6_findings.interpretation: Old fold results below are descriptive and already exposed. The March 5 Predictorium statement motivates policy; it does not independently establish Connectome timestamp order.

top6_findings.finding: Strong historical internal GRU evidence includes a warm-start T3 F0 control at WP .681154 and a fixed oldZ4 student/HFT Q8 pair at .683494 on F0; both are old-fold evaluations, not official valid.

evidence.excerpt: F0 WP .68115416 versus Q8 .67382636 on matched rows.

top6_findings.interpretation: The Q8 artifact is an evaluation of a fixed .5/.5 student/HFT blend, not a new fit. T3 is a warm-started, teacher-cache-dependent student and does not isolate distillation, initialization or optimizer effects.

top6_findings.finding: The traced best public score is TL3 at .66832, a three-model ensemble from a user-supplied 100-submission trace.
top6_findings.interpretation: This is public leaderboard evidence, not official valid or private evidence. Portal payload bytes are unverified. The blend combines one distilled 211-feature GRU and two tied-lead 263-feature GRUs; it is not one plain-GRU recipe.

top6_findings.finding: HPO trial 35 is the strongest specifically recoverable H384 teacher recipe: two-fold adjusted objective .6687635, with old fold1 .6695942 and fold0 .6799267.

evidence.excerpt: Fold1 objective, fold0 reduced by difficulty offset; folds2/3 confirmation.

top6_findings.interpretation: This is a tunable historical lead, not a validated optimum: the objective uses two old folds; reported raw delta intervals include zero. The report's roughly +.0012 width comparison over four old folds is narrow and uncertain.

top6_findings.finding: The canonical scratch H256x2 recipe reaches about .666-.667 on old fold1; a six-epoch run peaks at epoch 3 then degrades to about .662 and .649.

evidence.excerpt: Fold1 reaches about .666 at epochs 2-3; six-epoch path peaks .6671 at epoch 3 then declines.

top6_findings.interpretation: This supports a short-run scratch control and warns against assuming more epochs help this particular recipe. It is not a general epoch ceiling.

top6_findings.finding: A .7181503 strict425 pair is the highest scalar found, but it is not comparable evidence for the main task or public/private quality.

evidence.excerpt: wave12 pair .7181503 vs teacher .7153250; organizer pretraining uncertified.

top6_findings.interpretation: It reuses fold0 on a 425-sequence/123-chain true-mask slice, has no train holdout, and its difference from direct supervision has an interval crossing zero. The underlying result path is absent from this HEAD; no public/private estimate is stated. Do not select it over better-matched evidence by scalar alone.

galam_boundary.statement: Keep historical plain-GRU recipes distinct from the new schematic GALAM-GRU reconstruction.
galam_boundary.reason: Source-traced GALAM packet identifies visible blocks and example configurations but does not establish original dimensions, original training recipe, exact source identity or fidelity of hyperparameters. No plain-GRU historical hyperparameter is proven optimal for GALAM.

unknowns: No historical result in this audit was re-run under the current official train-only fit / independent official valid protocol.
The exact per-run normalization vectors and complete row/group ancestry for every old teacher/cache are artifact-bound; this report gives recipe semantics, not copied numeric arrays.
Trial35 raw event parameters and fold score records are recovered, but one standalone executable command and exact process/environment capture were not recovered here.
TL3 portal payload bytes and exact serving-side member payload identity remain unverified.
Strict425 underlying wave12 report is absent from this HEAD; only the summary in RECENT_OTHER_BRANCHES.md was available.
No current Connectome timestamp/order evidence is established by the Predictorium protocol statement or by seq_ix.
Original GALAM image dimensions/source and exact original training recipe are unknown; no exact reconstruction claim is supported.
The inspected source set is a bounded historical audit, not proof that no higher or stronger result exists elsewhere in all repository history.
